result.note: The softening itself is only likely, so the questions test the settled facts: the CERC draft of September 2025 and its tolerance bands.

questions.prompt: In September 2025, which body released draft rules requiring wind and solar developers to match their promised supply to the grid more closely, with penalties for deviations?
questions.explain: The Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (CERC) issued the draft grid-discipline rules in September 2025. In March 2026, the government asked the CERC to re-examine the penalties after developers warned that they would kill investment.
questions.source: Draft rules released by the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (CERC) in September 2025 aimed to force renewable players to match their promised supply to the grid.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about deviation tolerance bands for renewable energy projects, as reported in March 2026:
items: Under the existing rules, wind developers have a tolerance band of +/-15% around their promised supply.
The CERC draft proposed shrinking the solar tolerance band to +/-5% by 2026.
The CERC draft proposed bringing renewable tolerance bands to parity with conventional generators by 2028.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 3 is wrong. The draft proposed a gradual reduction that would reach the tolerance bands of conventional generators by 2031, not 2028. Developers estimated that the tighter bands could cause revenue losses of up to 48% because of the intermittent nature of renewables.
questions.source: Under the new proposal, tolerance bands would shrink to +/-10% for wind and +/-5% for solar by 2026 then gradually reduce until finally having the same tolerance bands as conventional generators by 2031.
